ops.d: List every namespaces in the subscription.
List the namespaces in a resource group.

features.t: Namespaces — create, list, get, update, delete (generic ARM catalog)
Tags
Scale (pricing tier)
x: Vyomi enforces the headline tier gates — a Basic namespace rejects topic creation and queues with sessions or duplicate detection enabled, and messaging units / premiumMessagingPartitions require a Premium namespace — but per-tier throughput, entity size and partition-COUNT limits are not otherwise modelled.

features.t: Shared access policies (authorizationRules) and their keys/connection strings (listKeys)
x: listKeys returns the same fixed simulated key pair every generic ARM resource's listKeys action does; it is not derived from the policy's configured rights.

features.t: Resource locks (Microsoft.Authorization/locks), scoped to this namespace, plus the Locks panel's Subscription / Resource group scope-switcher buttons
x: Enforcement is scoped to the exact locked resource (the namespace, or a queue/topic locked directly over the ARM API) — a lock does not cascade to block writes/deletes on a namespace's queues or topics the way a resource-group-scoped lock would in real ARM.

features.t: Namespace activity log
x: Only console/SDK-triggered mutations made since the simulation booted are recorded (no historical backfill); severity/category filtering and the 7/30/90-day timespan picker are not modelled, and `caller` is a fixed placeholder identity rather than the real signed-in principal.

features.t: Activity log toolbar actions that open a separate Azure product or portal chrome: Activity/Export Activity Logs/Insights/Pin current filters, and Locks'/Activity log's Feedback
x: 'Activity' (the timespan picker's companion action) and 'Pin current filters' write to the signed-in user's Azure Dashboard, a separate resource type (Microsoft.Portal/dashboards) Vyomi does not model; 'Export Activity Logs' configures the SUBSCRIPTION's own continuous Activity Log export (a Microsoft.Insights/diagnosticSettings extension scoped to '/subscriptions/{sub}', not to this namespace — a different resource than the namespace's own Diagnostic settings page, which IS real, see azure.servicebus.namespace.diagnosticsettings) and is not wired up; 'Insights' opens the Service Bus Insights workbook (Microsoft.Insights/workbooks pre-authored by Microsoft, not user data) which is not modeled; 'Feedback' posts to a real Microsoft telemetry endpoint outside the simulator.

features.t: Properties (read-only resource summary)
Export template (ARM template)
x: Only the ARM Template tab is generated from the namespace's real properties; Bicep and Terraform export are not modeled.

features.t: Access control (IAM) on a namespace: role assignments and built-in role definitions over ARM, plus Check access / My access
x: Role assignments and role definitions are real ARM resources (Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments, roleDefinitions), and Check access / My access run the real wildcard + scope-inheritance + notActions + explicit-deny decision — all ENFORCED scoped to this namespace (plus its subscription/resource-group ancestors, matching real Azure's inherited-access view); Roles stays subscription-wide, which matches real Azure (built-in role definitions are listed tenant-wide too). Deny assignments and Classic administrators remain an honest gap — Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management and the legacy Azure Service Management administrator list are not modelled. Update: the Deny assignments list, Classic administrators (a read-only list of the subscription's account administrator, like the real API) and My access (the simulated signed-in principal, evaluated with checkAccess) are now real shared tabs (azure.common.*); the gap wording above predates them.

features.t: Identity (system-assigned managed identity)
x: User assigned identities are real: the identity block can reference Microsoft.ManagedIdentity/userAssignedIdentities resources, an unknown reference is rejected with 400 ResourceNotFound and the attached identity's principalId/clientId are resolved from that resource.

features.t: Networking (network rule sets)
x: Premium namespaces only: networkRuleSets/default (public network access, default action, IP rules, virtual network rules whose subnet must exist and carry the Microsoft.ServiceBus service endpoint) is a validated ARM resource. Rules are not evaluated against data-plane connections.

features.t: Encryption (customer-managed key)
x: Premium namespaces only; requires a managed identity and a Key Vault that exists in this subscription. The key is looked up in the Key Vault keys data plane (400 KeyVaultKeyNotFound / KeyVaultKeyDisabled); that store is one keyspace shared by all vaults, so the lookup is by key name, not per vault; messages are not re-encrypted or blocked when the key is disabled.

features.t: Geo-disaster recovery (paired namespaces + alias failover)
x: Pairing (disasterRecoveryConfigs), role (Primary/Secondary) and FailOver are real ARM state, ENFORCED: both namespaces of a pairing must exist, differ, and be Premium tier, and FailOver must be invoked from the Secondary's own path — exactly like real Service Bus (core/azure_arm_core.AzureArm._servicebus_georecovery).

features.t: Diagnostic settings (Microsoft.Insights/diagnosticSettings, scoped to this namespace)
x: Logs/metrics are never actually delivered to the configured destination (workspace, storage account or event hub) — there is no agent/telemetry pipeline, so the setting is stored and validated exactly as the real resource requires but nothing flows.

features.t: Alert rules (Microsoft.Insights/metricAlerts, scoped to this namespace)
x: A metric alert rule is a real, resource-group-scoped ARM resource that round-trips (create/list/delete, enabled/disabled, condition, severity) exactly as configured, scoped to this namespace via properties.scopes — but there is no metrics pipeline to evaluate the condition against, so a rule never actually fires or notifies an action group.

features.t: Insights and Metrics charts on a namespace
x: Insights and Metrics are the shared per-resource panels (azure.common.resource_monitoring): the only metric is the namespace's own Activity-log operation count, charted over the last 24 hours. Message-count, throttling and size metrics are not sampled or retained over time anywhere in Vyomi (only the live point-in-time counts on the Overview/Queues/Topics pages). The pre-authored Microsoft Insights workbook is not modelled.

features.t: Logs (a Log Analytics query scoped to this namespace)
x: Runs the same real KQL pass-through (POST .../workspaces/{ws}/api/query) the Monitor service's own Logs page uses, defaulted to this namespace's own AzureActivity rows (ResourceId filter) — but only the built-in AzureActivity table returns real data (core/azure_operationalinsights_core.py); there is no Service Bus-specific resource-diagnostic table (e.g. OperationalLogs) to query even once a Diagnostic setting routes logs to a workspace, since nothing is actually delivered there (azure.servicebus.namespace.diagnosticsettings).

features.t: Diagnose and solve problems, Events, Tasks
x: 'Diagnose and solve problems' runs Microsoft's own troubleshooting detectors against Azure's internal health-signal pipeline (Resource Health + Application Insights correlation) — there is no local analog to correlate against. 'Events' wires this namespace up as an Event Grid system-topic source (Microsoft.EventGrid/systemTopics with topicType Microsoft.ServiceBus.*), a cross-service subscription flow not modeled for Service Bus specifically. 'Tasks' links to Azure Automation runbooks, which need a live Microsoft backend. Support + Troubleshooting and Resource health are the shared panels (azure.common.support, azure.common.resource_health).

features.t: Queues — create, list, get, update, delete (ARM sub-resource of the namespace)
x: maxDeliveryCount, enablePartitioning and the auto-delete-on-idle/forwarding toggles round-trip through ARM exactly as configured, but only defaultMessageTimeToLive, lockDuration and dead-lettering-on-expiration are enforced by the data plane (see azure.servicebus.queue.explorer). requiresSession and requiresDuplicateDetection round-trip too, except Vyomi now rejects setting either one true on a Basic-tier namespace's queue (see azure.servicebus.namespace.scale).

features.t: Topics — create, list, get, update, delete (ARM sub-resource of the namespace)
x: Topic subscriptions and their SQL filter rules are not modeled in this console — only the topic resource itself round-trips. Vyomi rejects creating a topic on a Basic-tier namespace (see azure.servicebus.namespace.scale), matching real Service Bus.

features.t: Service Bus Explorer — send, peek, receive, complete, defer and move to dead letter on a queue
x: The Service Bus data plane is a simplified, invented REST surface (the real Service Bus data plane is AMQP-only and can't cross the relay) — complete/defer/dead-letter act by sequence number directly rather than the SDK's lock-token dance, and 'Peek next messages' re-peeks the same backlog rather than paging through it.
